title: COUNT: numbers only, and what it skips

screens.prompt: In B8, count how many readings in B2:B7 are really numbers.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close the bracket: =COUNT(B2:B7).
hints.func-count: COUNT answers how many numbers there are; SUM answers how much they add up to, which is a different question.
hints.require-ref: Point COUNT at B2:B7. Numbers typed into the formula stop matching the sheet the moment a sample is re-measured.
hints.value: That is not how many numbers the column holds. Read down B2:B7 and ask of each cell whether it is a number.
hints.error: COUNT of a range never fails on text, but dividing its answer by zero returns #DIV/0!, and a call with no argument at all returns #VALUE!.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
COUNTA counts the labels and the text too, which is the question this screen is not asking
the readings added up are 35.7, not how many of them there are
COUNT with no argument has nothing to count
the readings typed into the formula, so the count stops following the sheet
the range stops at S-04, so the 15 in S-05 is left out
a count divided by zero returns #DIV/0!

docs.explain: Column B mixes things up on purpose: 12.5 in B2, the words n/a in B3, 8.2 in B4, an empty cell in B5, 15 in B6 and the text 7 in B7. COUNT walks the range and counts only the cells Excel holds as numbers, so it answers 3: the 12.5, the 8.2 and the 15. The n/a is text and is skipped, the blank in B5 is nothing at all, and the 7 in B7 is text because it was typed in with an apostrophe or pasted from a system that sends everything as text — it looks like a number and Excel does not treat it as one. SUM over the same range answers 35.7, which is why a count that comes back short is the fastest way to find cells that arrived as text.

errors.text: The count was divided by zero, usually because a formula was filled into a row whose divisor is still empty.
COUNT was called with no argument at all, as in =COUNT(). It needs at least one range or value to look at.

docs.atWork: Importing a supplier's stock file, where some quantities arrive as text and a count that disagrees with the row total is how you find them.
docs.outcome: Count the cells that hold real numbers, and know why the total looks one short.
